source_name: NBS — Digitálna prevádzková odolnosť finančného sektora (DORA)
why_relevant: NBS's dedicated DORA landing page: SK supervisory expectations, ICT third-party register reporting, incident reporting channels and national accompanying legislation (novela zákona č. 747/2004 Z. z.). The canonical SK-side view of a directly applicable EU regulation.

source_name: NBS — Okamžité platby a overenie prijímateľa (Instant Payments Regulation hub)
why_relevant: NBS's SK-facing explanation of Regulation (EU) 2024/886 obligations and the 9 Jan 2025 / 9 Oct 2025 deadlines, incl. Verification of Payee and fee-parity rules as applied to Slovak PSPs.

source_name: NBS — Legislatíva AML/CFT
why_relevant: Tracks the SK landing of the EU AML package (AMLR 2024/1624 applicable 10 July 2027, AMLD6, AMLA), including which EBA AML guidelines NBS applies and the replacement of zákon č. 297/2008 Z. z.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR — Transposition of EU Directives
why_relevant: The ministry that owns financial-services transposition publishes its own status list of directives it is responsible for transposing — the earliest official SK-side signal of a coming implementing act (e.g. PSD3/PSR, CRD6, AMLD6).

source_name: Slov-Lex — právny a informačný portál (e-Zbierka, legislatívny proces)
source_subtype: national legal gazette / legislative process portal
why_relevant: Every SK act transposing an EU directive must carry a transposition annex naming the EU act and OJ reference; Slov-Lex holds the consolidated texts and the pre-legislative comment procedure (medzirezortné pripomienkové konanie) where draft transposition bills appear first.

source_name: ECB — Instant Payments Regulation page
why_relevant: ECB's authoritative reading of the IPR obligation timeline (reachability, sending, VoP, sanctions screening) that binds euro-area — hence all Slovak — PSPs, plus TIPS-side implementation implications.

source_name: European Payments Council — Verification of Payee scheme rulebook & SCT Inst rulebook consultations
why_relevant: The IPR's VoP and instant-payment obligations are operationalised through EPC scheme rulebooks and their public consultations; SK banks adhere as scheme participants, so rulebook change cycles set real SK implementation deadlines beyond the legal text.

source_name: European Commission — NIS2 Directive implementation in Slovakia (digital-strategy portal)
why_relevant: Commission-maintained per-country transposition page naming the exact SK act (zákon č. 366/2024 Z. z., in force 1 Jan 2025) and authority. Model for how EU portals publish SK-specific transposition facts relevant to DORA/NIS2 overlap for banks.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) — novinky / positions on EU rules
why_relevant: The only banking-industry association in SK; comments on EU directives (e.g. security-of-payments directive coverage) and issues sector recommendations. Reveals how EU deadlines are being operationalised and where the sector pushes back. Registered in the EU Transparency Register.

source_name: SK professional-services regulatory trackers (PwC SK, ULC, Avris, Prosman & Pavlovič, Highgate)
why_relevant: Slovak law/advisory firms publish the most explicit SK-language mapping of EU acts to national deadlines and to which SK statute changes (DORA and the 747/2004 amendment, AML package, PSD3/PSR transition periods). Useful for lead-finding and terminology, must be verified against primary sources.

source_name: NBS — Európske právo v oblasti poskytovania platobných služieb (NBS working paper/guide)
why_relevant: NBS-published SK-language treatment of EU payment-services law, including the PSD3/PSR proposals and the European Parliament's April 2024 legislative resolution — rare authoritative SK terminology source for the payments legal stack.

source_name: Finančná spravodajská jednotka (FSJ), Prezídium Policajného zboru — hlavná stránka
why_relevant: Slovak FIU and AML supervisory/administrative authority under §5 zákona 297/2008; the primary publisher of AML guidance, obligations, sanctions practice and reporting rules that bind banks and payment institutions. Root hub for all FSJ subpages (usmernenia, povinnosti a sankcie, výročné správy, NHR).

source_name: FSJ — Povinnosti a sankcie (obligations of obliged entities, fine ranges)
why_relevant: States the concrete statutory duties (CDD, STR/NOO reporting, 5-year retention, programme vlastnej činnosti, training) and the penalty ladder (up to EUR 1m generally; up to EUR 5m or 10% turnover for banks/financial institutions; personal fines for board members) — the compliance-cost baseline for banks and PSPs.

source_name: FSJ — usmernenia a stanoviská (PDF guidance library, /fsj_biro/usmernenia/)
why_relevant: The FIU issues written usmernenia/stanoviská interpreting the AML Act for obliged entities (e.g. exemptions from the §18 confidentiality duty; non-face-to-face client identification and use of §12). These are the operative interpretations banks and payment firms must implement; they change with amendments.

source_name: FSJ — výročné správy (FIU annual reports)
why_relevant: Annual FIU reports carry STR/NOO volumes by sector, inspection counts at banks and payment institutions, sanctioning statistics and typologies — the best quantitative time series on AML supervisory pressure in SK.

source_name: Správa z III. kola národného hodnotenia rizík ML/TF (National Risk Assessment, 3rd round)
why_relevant: The NRA sets the risk ratings that drive supervisory intensity and sectoral obligations for banks, payment institutions and VASPs; 3rd round covers 2020-2023. Directly predicts where inspections and new requirements land.

source_name: Národná stratégia boja proti legalizácii výnosov z trestnej činnosti, financovaniu terorizmu a proliferácie (do 2030)
why_relevant: Government-approved AML/CFT/CPF strategy (approved by uznesenie vlády č. 472/2025 per secondary reporting) — forward-looking action plan with owners and deadlines; the best single predictor of upcoming SK AML regulatory workstreams.

source_name: FSJ — informačné materiály pre povinné osoby (kpo/u24 PDF series)
why_relevant: Numbered FSJ briefing sheets for obliged entities covering AML Act amendments and risk-assessment duties; a fast-moving channel where new obligations and effective dates appear before consolidated guidance.

source_name: Slov-Lex — zákon č. 297/2008 Z. z. (AML zákon), konsolidované znenie
why_relevant: Authoritative consolidated text and amendment history of the Slovak AML Act, including the 2026 amendment (73/2026 Z. z.). Amendment metadata gives exact effective dates — the deadline backbone for banks and payment institutions.

source_name: Slov-Lex — legislatívny proces (LP/PI): AML draft laws and consultations
why_relevant: Pripomienkové konanie portal: where MV SR files AML drafts and predbežné informácie before adoption — e.g. LP/2025/518 (AML amendment, shortened consultation Oct 2025) and PI/2026/51 (planned full replacement of 297/2008 aligned to the EU AML Regulation, effective ~10 July 2027). Earliest legal warning of new obligations and deadlines.

source_name: NR SR (parlament) — parlamentná tlač k novelám AML zákona
why_relevant: Parliamentary prints carry dôvodová správa (explanatory memorandum), doložka vplyvov and amendment stages for AML and sanctions bills — needed to date obligations and read legislative intent before publication in Zbierka.

source_name: NBS — AML/CFT dohľad nad finančným trhom (AML supervision section)
why_relevant: NBS runs AML/CFT supervision of the financial market under zák. 747/2004 in parallel with FSJ's §5 supervision; this dedicated AML section (separate from prudential output) hosts metodické usmernenia a stanoviská, legislatíva AML/CFT, ML/TF risk assessment and AML supervisory cooperation pages relevant to banks and payment institutions.

source_name: NBS — Vestník NBS: metodické usmernenia (AML and payment-institution ICS)
why_relevant: The Vestník is the formal publication channel for NBS metodické usmernenia (e.g. MU 3/2019, 4/2019, MU 3/2023; MU 4/2014 on the internal control system of payment institutions and e-money institutions), which set expected AML control standards for banks and PSPs.

source_name: NBS — Výroky právoplatných rozhodnutí (published enforcement decisions)
why_relevant: Public register of final (and enforceable non-final) supervisory decisions, including AML fines against banks — e.g. a EUR 100,000 fine on a bank branch for CDD/UBO and unusual-transaction failures, final 22 May 2026 per press reporting. The only systematic view of actual AML enforcement severity in SK.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR — oblasť medzinárodných sankcií EÚ/OSN
why_relevant: MF SR is the competent authority hub for financial sanctions implementation under zákon 289/2016 Z. z.; hosts sanctions-list pages, guidance on the law, and a curated list of key sanctions websites. Asset-freeze and reporting duties fall directly on banks and payment institutions.

source_name: MZV SR — Medzinárodné sankcie / EU sanctions
why_relevant: Foreign ministry publishes consolidated Slovak-language texts of individual sanctions regimes and overviews of listed persons/entities; complements MF SR on the foreign-policy side and is often first to reflect new EU packages nationally.

source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) — Slovak Republic country page and reports
why_relevant: MER adopted Sep 2020 put SK in enhanced follow-up; FURs adopted Nov 2022, Dec 2023 and Dec 2024 with technical-compliance re-ratings (reported as 5 C / 23 LC / 12 PC after the 2024 round). MONEYVAL announced in Jan 2026 that SK exits the 5th-round follow-up process, with the 6th-round on-site visit scheduled for October 2028 — a hard, datable driver of future SK AML reform.

source_name: FATF-GAFI — Slovak Republic country page and FSRB follow-up reports
why_relevant: FATF mirrors MONEYVAL outputs for SK and hosts the FUR PDFs plus Recommendation-level ratings (incl. R.26 on regulation/supervision of financial institutions). Also the authoritative place for any grey-list risk signal affecting SK-facing correspondent banking.

source_name: AMLA — Authority for Anti-Money Laundering and CFT (EU, Frankfurt)
why_relevant: The EU Single Rulebook applies from 10 July 2027 and AMLA begins direct supervision of up to ~40 high-risk credit/financial institutions (including payment and e-money institutions and CASPs) from 2028; most Level 2/3 measures are due by 10 July 2026. This supersedes large parts of the SK national AML regime — including the planned full replacement of zákon 297/2008.
